questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The group of students, B. along with the professor, C. were discussing the new findings D. in the research lab.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence lies in a lack of subject-verb agreement within the segment "**were discussing the new findings**."
 
• The true subject of the sentence is the singular collective noun "**group**" (in the phrase "The group of students").
 
• Interrupting phrases introduced by "along with," "as well as," or "in addition to" do not change the number of the subject. Therefore, the singular subject "group" still requires a singular verb.
 
• The plural helping verb "**were**" must be changed to the singular "**was**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in the segment **were discussing the new findings**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The group of students, along with the professor, **was** discussing the new findings in the research lab."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The group of students** – This segment is grammatically correct. It establishes the singular subject of the sentence.
 
• **along with the professor** – This segment is correct. It acts as an interrupting prepositional phrase that provides extra information but does not affect the verb's conjugation.
 
• **in the research lab.** – This segment is grammatically correct. It is a well-formed prepositional phrase functioning as an adverb of place.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. She spoke B. so fastly that C. I could barely understand D. what she was saying.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary error in the sentence lies in the use of the word "**fastly**."
 
• "Fastly" is not a valid word in standard English. The word "**fast**" is an irregular adverb, meaning it functions as both an adjective and an adverb without needing the "-ly" suffix.
 
• Therefore, the correct adverbial form to describe how she spoke is simply "**fast**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in the segment **so fastly that**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She spoke **so fast that** I could barely understand what she was saying."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **She spoke** – This segment is grammatically correct. It establishes a clear subject and a past tense verb.
 
• **I could barely understand** – This segment is correct. "Barely" is used correctly as an adverb modifying the verb phrase "could understand."
 
• **what she was saying.** – This segment is correct. It functions perfectly as a noun clause acting as the direct object of "understand."

• The word **"Retired"** refers to someone who has stopped working, usually after reaching a certain age, or has withdrawn from an active life. (सेवानिवृत्त)
 
 
• **Example:** After working for 40 years, he finally retired and decided to travel the world.
 
 
• **"Active"**, on the other hand, means someone who is energetic, engaged, or involved in physical or mental activities. It is the direct opposite of being retired or withdrawn. (सक्रिय)
 
 
• **Example:** Despite being over 70, she remains active by participating in community events and yoga classes.
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the antonym of **"Retired"** is **"Active"**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The student said, "I have been reading this book for a month, but I still do not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part."

options.text: The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
The student said that he has been reading this bookfor a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.
The student said that he had been reading this book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The student said, "I have been reading this book for a month, but I still do not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"have been reading" becomes "had been reading"**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense, the **Present Perfect Continuous** tense ("have been reading") changes to the **Past Perfect Continuous** tense ("had been reading").
 
 
 
• **"this book" becomes "that book"**
 
 
• In indirect speech, words expressing nearness in time or place change to words expressing distance. "This" becomes **"that."**
 
 
 
• **"do not understand" becomes "did not understand"**
 
 
• The **Simple Present** tense ("do not understand") changes to the **Simple Past** tense ("did not understand").
 
 
 
• **"which is" becomes "which was"**
 
 
• Similarly, the **Simple Present** verb "is" changes to the **Simple Past** verb "was."
 
 
 
• **"I" becomes "he"**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun "I" changes to the third-person pronoun "he" to match the subject (the student).
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "...he has been reading this book... does not understand... which is..." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the present tenses to past tenses and fails to change "this" to "that."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "...reading this book..." 
 
 
• Incorrect solely because it retains the word "this" instead of changing it to "that."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "...does not understand the last chapter, which is..." 
 
 
• Incorrect because while it fixes the first half of the sentence, it fails to backshift the verbs in the second half ("does not understand" and "is" should be in the past tense).

Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

All the **__jury members was divided__** in their opinions.

options.text: All the jury member were divided
All the jury members were divided
All the jury were divided between their opinions
All juries have divided in their opinions

questions.solution:

 **__Key Points__**
 
 

__
 
• The subject of the sentence, **"jury members,"** is plural. Therefore, the verb must also be in the plural form to maintain subject-verb agreement.
 
• **Option 1:** "All the jury member were divided" is incorrect because "member" is singular, which does not match the plural subject "jury members."
 
• **Option 3:** "All the jury were divided between their opinions" is incorrect because "jury" is treated as a collective noun, and "between their opinions" is not grammatically accurate in this context.
 
• **Option 4:** "All juries have divided in their opinions" is incorrect because "juries" refers to multiple groups of jury, which changes the meaning of the sentence.

 Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 
 **Complete Sentence:** *"All the jury members were divided in their opinions."*

 **Additional Information__**
 
 

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** It is essential to match the subject and verb in number. A plural subject requires a plural verb, and a singular subject requires a singular verb.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

You must finish your homework.

options.text: Your homework must be finished by you.
Your homework must being finished by you.
Your homework must have been finished by you.
Your homework is must be finished by you.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice: "You must finish your homework." 
 
• To convert it to passive voice, the object of the active sentence ("your homework") becomes the subject of the passive sentence. 
 
• The modal "must" remains the same, and the verb "finish" changes to its past participle form "finished." 
 
• The correct structure is: "Your homework must be finished by you." 
 
• Incorrect options: 
 
 
• **Option 2: **"Your homework must being finished by you." – Incorrect because "must being" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 3: **"Your homework must have been finished by you." – Incorrect because it changes the meaning and tense of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"Your homework is must be finished by you." – Incorrect because it includes an extra verb ("is") that makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Your homework must be finished by you."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Active voice:** The subject performs the action (e.g., "You must finish your homework"). 
 
• **Passive voice:** The object becomes the subject, and the focus shifts to the action being done (e.g., "Your homework must be finished by you"). 
 
• **Structure for passive voice with modals:** Modal + be + past participle.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The new intern had forgotten to lock the laboratory door before leaving.

options.text: The laboratory door was forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
The laboratory door had been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
The laboratory door has been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
The laboratory door had forgotten to lock by the new intern before leaving.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The new intern had forgotten to lock the laboratory door before leaving."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the laboratory door" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "had forgotten" to "had been forgotten" (past perfect passive).
 
• Ensure the rest of the sentence remains grammatically correct and retains its original meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The laboratory door had been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The laboratory door was forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving." – Incorrect because "was" is used instead of "had been," which is required for past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 3: **"The laboratory door has been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive instead of past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"The laboratory door had forgotten to lock by the new intern before leaving." – Incorrect structure; "had forgotten" must apply to the subject (intern), not the object (door).

questions.question: Identify the voice in "Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Identification of the Voice:***

 
 
• The phrase uses the past participle **"conceived."** In the full context of the sentence, it implies that "Chaturanga was initially conceived..."
 
• In **Passive Voice**, the subject of the sentence (Chaturanga) is the receiver of the action, not the doer. The game did not "conceive" itself; it was conceived by people/creators.
 
 
 
• ***Structural Analysis:***
 
 
• **Active Voice equivalent**: "Creators initially conceived Chaturanga as a strategic simulation..." (The subject performs the action).
 
• **Passive Voice (this phrase)**: "Initially conceived..." (The focus is on the thing being created/conceived).
 
 
 
• ***Analysis of Other Options:***
 
 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the subject is not performing the action of conceiving.
 
• **Option 3**: **Middle Voice** is a grammatical voice where the subject both performs and is affected by the action (e.g., "The door opened"). This does not apply here.
 
• **Option 4**: **Causative Voice** indicates that the subject causes someone else to do something (e.g., "I had my hair cut"). This is not present in the phrase.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Passive voice.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Utility**: Authors often use passive voice when the actor (the person who conceived the game) is unknown, irrelevant, or less important than the object (the game itself).
 
• **Past Participle as Adjective**: In this specific phrase, "conceived" acts as a participle modifying "chaturanga," but its underlying grammatical relationship to the noun remains passive.

questions.question: According to the passage, what factor in recent years has accelerated chess talent development in India?

The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Digital Acceleration:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly mentions: **"Digital platforms have further accelerated talent development..."** It explains that these platforms allow young aspirants to play against (spar with) grandmasters from all over the world.
 
 
 
• ***Strategic Growth:***
 
 
• The text notes that this global interaction helps in **"refining their strategic acumen from an early age,"** moving beyond just local tournaments or traditional coaching.
 
 
 
• ***Analysis of Other Options:***
 
 
• **Option 1**: The passage mentions academies and grassroots initiatives, but not "board game shops" as a primary factor.
 
• **Option 3**: While grassroots initiatives are mentioned, the passage does not state that chess programs are "mandatory" in schools.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the passage highlights an **increased** presence and success in international events like the Chess Olympiad.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Digital platforms allowing global practice.**

• **Strategic Acumen**: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions in a complex environment (like a chess game).
 
• **Cradle of Chess**: A reference to India being the birthplace of the original game, "chaturanga."

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

The interior designer received a __________ from her client for choosing furniture that would perfectly __________ the walls and floors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. compliment, complement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"compliment"** refers to a polite expression of praise or admiration. (प्रशंसा या तारीफ)
 
 
• **Example:** She received a compliment on her beautiful dress.
 
 
• The word **"complement"** refers to something that completes or goes well with something else. (पूरक)
 
 
• **Example:** The new curtains perfectly complement the color of the walls.
 
 
• In the given sentence, "compliment" and "complement" are the correct words because the designer received praise (compliment) for choosing furniture that perfectly matched or completed (complemented) the walls and floors.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. compliment, complement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: counsel, council**
 
 
• **"Counsel"** means advice or guidance, typically given formally. (सलाह)
 
• **Example:** She sought counsel from her mentor before making the decision.
 
• **"Council"** refers to an assembly or advisory group formed to discuss and decide on important matters. (परिषद)
 
• **Example:** The city council voted on the new zoning regulations.
 
• These words do not fit the context of the sentence, as the sentence refers to praise and matching, not advice or an assembly.
 
 

 
• **Option 2: complement, compliment**
 
 
• This option has the correct words but in the wrong order. The sentence requires "compliment" first and "complement" second to make sense in the given context.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: council, counsel**
 
 
• This option also uses "council" and "counsel," which refer to a group or advice, respectively. These do not suit the context of the sentence.
